newsitem.title: UK: UK natural gas weakens ahead of Transco tender.
newsitem.headline: UK natural gas weakens ahead of Transco tender.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices were weaker on Friday amid speculation over the size of an imminent Transco tender to sell natural gas.

The tender finally arrived after most traders had left their offices and it constituted an offer to sell 5.381 terawatt-hours (TWH,) or slightly more than 180 million therms, on July 1 within existing storage, according to a copy of the tender document.
Of this total, 0.184 TWH will be made available at Partington and 5.197 TWH at the Rough storage facility.
Traders had earlier expected the tender to be a phased disposal of between 80 and 120 million therms between July and September, both within storage as well as at the NBP.
Most deals during the day were softer. The gas year changed hands at 12.90 pence per therm, a fall of around a tenth of a penny, and the first half of next year was traded at 13.90 and 13.95 pence.
The summer of next year was also traded, fetching 10.8 pence per therm, and another deal was executed for Q1+Q2 of 1999 at 14.20 pence.
Prompt gas was also softer after traders were warned by Transco ahead of the tender that it would be executed on July 1 instead of through the summer.
But one regular player said: "There is a feeling that the tender will have less overall impact than the phased sale because it will just be the case of gas changing hands within storage."
The IPE was busy in the morning, with a relatively healthy 250 lots traded, but business then dried up in the afteroon.
